notes:
Account snapshot: Aurora builds a verticalized search product for regulated enterprise docs (legal, contracts, policy). They already run keyword search + heuristics; want to layer embeddings + ML reranker to improve precision for top-K. Key asks: handle 100M+ vectors, sub-150ms P95 query latency for user-facing search, cost per query under $0.02 at target QPS, and connector flexibility to use pgvector for local ops but fall back to managed vector DBs for spikes.

Key quotes / call snippets:
- CTO: "We need better top-K precision; it's fine if recall is slightly lower as long as top results are near-perfect."
- Head of Search: "If we can't scale to 100M efficiently we won't proceed. Show us memory + cost numbers."

Integration/connector requirements (from convo):
- Support for pgvector + PostgreSQL-based ingest (CDC/streaming) and an option to push to Pinecone/Weaviate for burst capacity.
- Filtering by contract metadata (date, jurisdiction, client_id) with vector + boolean hybrid queries.
- ANN choice: HNSW with predictable memory footprint; ability to tune ef/search and ef/build.
- Incremental/nearline indexing: low-latency updates for 500-1k docs/day, and bulk reindex path for migrations.
- Batch embedding pipeline with tokenization hints and per-document dimension (d=1536 preferred); allow multi-model embedding backends.
- Reranker path: retrieve 20-50 candidates, run a small cross-encoder reranker (local or dedicated) to reorder top-5; budget for reranker QPS at peak.

POC success criteria (agreed):
- Ingest 10M sample vectors end-to-end with connectors and confirm 95th latency <200ms for single-shot retrieval + rerank (demo with 5 replicates).
- Memory footprint and cost per query model documented for 10M -> extrapolate to 100M.
- Security checklist signed: SSO + KMS integration test, audit log sample export.
- Connector validation: pgvector performs within 20% of managed service for read latency on their infra.

Commercial notes: Aurora prefers reserved capacity for predictable run-rate; open to Dedicated pools if host-managed meets data residency. Legal asks for region tenancy and the ability to bring own KMS. Primary competitor in their evaluation is Pinecone for managed simplicity and Elastic for hybrid text+vector filtering.

AE next actions (Jordan): share cost model template, request infra sizing from Aurora, schedule pgvector perf test with their infra team, sync on legal questions (drive link).
requirements_summary: Scale: 100M+ vectors target; ingest pattern: daily micro-batches + occasional bulk; latency target: <=150ms P95 for retrieval-only, <=250ms P95 retrieval+rerank; cost sensitivity: medium (willing to invest for quality but need predictable per-query economics); models: embeddings d=1536 (open models), reranker: cross-encoder small-medium LLM (optimize product recommended); connectors: pgvector primary, optional Pinecone/Weaviate connector for burst, Elastic for boolean+text filtering; features: metadata filters, vector+filter hybrid queries, incremental updates, rebalancing/rehash workflow, metrics hooks for latency/cost per route; SLOs: canary rollout, automatic fallback to cheaper model variant when load spikes.
unique_considerations: Aurora operates in regulated contracts space: some tenants require EU residency. They may run private deployment for high-value enterprise customers and hosted for smaller accounts. Team cares a lot about deterministic memory use (HNSW params) and a reproducible cost model for reranker QPS. They also asked about automated model fallbacks when high latency observed.
